types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A legally constituted group of people with a shared purpose, such as a company or agency. Also called Company, Corporation, Enterprise, Firm. Examples: Google.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: Exact match for the OIE type and the mention "Google".

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: Cooperative
candidates.comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.embedding_query_text: MappingService: A digital platform that provides geographic maps and satellite imagery to users. Also called MapService, GeospatialPlatform, SatelliteMapProvider. Examples: Google Earth.

chosen_type.label: MappingService
chosen_type.definition: A digital platform that provides geographic maps and satellite imagery to users.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate matches a mapping service; a new subclass of Service (Intangible) is needed.

candidates.label: CableOrSatelliteService
candidates.comment: A CableOrSatelliteService is a Service that provides access to media programming, such as TV or radio, delivered via cable or satellite infrastructure. Also called pay TV service, satellite radio provider, broadcast subscription service. Examples: Comcast Xfinity, DirecTV, SiriusXM Satellite Radio.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

candidates.label: BroadcastService
candidates.comment: A BroadcastService is a Service that delivers content via broadcast, either over the air or online. Also called broadcasting service, media transmission service, content delivery service. Examples: a national television network, a satellite radio provider, an internet radio service.

candidates.label: TaxiService
candidates.comment: A local business or service offering vehicles for hire with drivers for local transportation, typically charging based on distance. Also called cab company, taxi provider, ride-hailing service. Examples: 'Yellow Cab Co.', 'Uber', 'Lyft', a local taxi firm. Distinct from Taxi, which refers to an instance of the service or the vehicle itself.

candidates.label: GeospatialGeometry
candidates.comment: GeospatialGeometry is an Intangible supertype of GeoShape, designed to accommodate definitions from Geo-Spatial best practices. Also called spatial geometry, geographic feature. Examples: A GeoShape, a KML polygon, a GeoJSON object.

types.embedding_query_text: AIImageGenerator: A software system that creates visual images from textual prompts using artificial intelligence. Also called GenerativeAI, ImageSynthesisTool, TextToImageModel. Examples: Nano Banana 2.

chosen_type.label: SoftwareApplication
chosen_type.justification: AI image generators are software applications; this broader class still captures the essential nature.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: ImageGallery
candidates.comment: An ImageGallery is a collection page web page type specifically designed to display a collection of images. Also called photo gallery, picture album, visual collection page. Examples: a wedding photo gallery, a portfolio of landscape images, a product image carousel. Distinct from VideoGallery, which displays videos, and MediaGallery, which is a more general type.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

types.embedding_query_text: MediaOutlet: An organization that produces and distributes news or informational content. Also called NewsOrganization, Press, JournalisticOutlet. Examples: BBC Verify.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Matches the media outlet concept and the example "BBC Verify".

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: AdvertiserContentArticle
candidates.comment: An AdvertiserContentArticle is an Article that has been paid for or produced to the specifications of an external entity. Also called sponsored article, advertorial, native advertising, paid content. Examples: A blog post promoting a product written by an influencer, a sponsored news segment, an article funded by a brand. Distinct from NewsArticle, which is typically produced by independent journalists.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: MediaReview
candidates.comment: A specialized review dedicated to evaluating online media content, often in the context of fact-checking and misinformation. Also called media fact-check, content authenticity review, misinformation analysis. Examples: a fact-check of a viral video, an analysis of a manipulated image, a review of a misleading news article. Distinct from Review, which is a general evaluation of any item or service.

candidates.label: MediaReviewItem
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an item or group of items treated as a single unit for evaluation within a MediaReview. Also called reviewed media unit, content item for review, media subject. Examples: a specific viral video, a collection of related images, a particular news clip.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called Individual, Human, Subject. Examples: Henk van Ess, Henry Ajder, Bill Greer, Trump.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for the OIE type and all listed mentions.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

types.embedding_query_text: NonProfitOrganization: An organization that operates for a public or social benefit without profit distribution. Also called Charity, NGO, Non‑governmentalOrganization. Examples: Common Space.

chosen_type.label: NGO
chosen_type.justification: NGO is the appropriate schema.org class for a non‑profit organization.

candidates.label: NGO
candidates.comment: An NGO (Non-governmental Organization) is a non-profit organization that operates independently of any government. Also called non-profit organization, charity, civil society organization. Examples: Doctors Without Borders, Amnesty International, local community charity. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category including for-profit entities.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: ArchiveOrganization
candidates.comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.embedding_query_text: ChatbotApplication: A software application that interacts with users through conversational text or voice, often powered by AI. Also called ConversationalAgent, VirtualAssistant, Chatbot. Examples: Gemini, Gemini chatbot app.

chosen_type.label: SoftwareApplication
chosen_type.justification: A chatbot is a software application; the generic class suffices.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: MobileApplication
candidates.comment: A software application designed specifically to function effectively on a mobile device. Also called mobile app, smartphone application, tablet app. Examples: "WhatsApp", "Instagram", "Google Maps app", a banking app. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a broader category for any software.

candidates.label: WebApplication
candidates.comment: A software application that runs on a web server and is accessed by users via a web browser. Also called web app, online application, browser-based application. Examples: Gmail, Google Docs, Facebook.

candidates.label: PronounceableText
candidates.comment: PronounceableText is a data type for text that can be pronounced, often including phonetic or linguistic information. Also called phonetic text, spoken text. Examples: "schema.org" (pronounced "schema dot org"), "résumé" (pronounced "rez-oo-may"), a word with its IPA transcription.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

types.embedding_query_text: ImageSearchFeature: A functionality within a software product that allows users to search using images. Also called VisualSearch, ImageRecognitionTool, LensFeature. Examples: Lens, Lens feature.

chosen_type.label: SearchAction
chosen_type.justification: The feature is a search action; this class best reflects the functionality.

candidates.label: ImageGallery
candidates.comment: An ImageGallery is a collection page web page type specifically designed to display a collection of images. Also called photo gallery, picture album, visual collection page. Examples: a wedding photo gallery, a portfolio of landscape images, a product image carousel. Distinct from VideoGallery, which displays videos, and MediaGallery, which is a more general type.

candidates.label: SearchAction
candidates.comment: The act of looking for an object or information, often using a search engine or database. Also called searching, querying, looking up, seeking. Examples: typing a query into Google, searching for a file on a computer, looking up a contact in a directory. Distinct from FindAction, which is the result of a search, not the act itself.

candidates.label: SearchResultsPage
candidates.comment: A web page displaying the results of a search query. Also called search results, SERP, query results page. Examples: Google search results page, Amazon product search results, a library catalog search page.

candidates.label: WarrantyScope
candidates.comment: An enumeration describing the range of services covered by a warranty in case of product defect or malfunction. Also called warranty coverage, guarantee scope, service level. Examples: "Parts and Labor - Bring In", "Labor - On Site", "Parts Only".

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

types.embedding_query_text: Landmark: A notable or historically significant physical structure or site. Also called Monument, IconicStructure, FamousSite. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Great Pyramid of Giza.

chosen_type.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
chosen_type.justification: Covers notable physical structures such as the Eiffel Tower and the Great Pyramid.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement, typically with administrative status. Also called UrbanArea, Metropolis, Municipality. Examples: Kyiv, Ukraine's capital.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: Exact match for the OIE type and the mention "Kyiv".

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign nation-state with defined territory and government. Also called Nation, State, Republic. Examples: Iran.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for the OIE type and the mention "Iran".

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

types.embedding_query_text: Border: A geographical line separating two political or administrative regions. Also called Boundary, Frontier, DividingLine. Examples: US-Mexico border.

chosen_type.label: Border
chosen_type.definition: A geographical line separating two political or administrative regions.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org class represents a border; the closest listed superclass is DefinedRegion.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

types.embedding_query_text: Region: A geographic area that may be defined by physical, cultural, or political characteristics. Also called Area, Zone, Territory. Examples: Gaza.

chosen_type.label: DefinedRegion
chosen_type.justification: The term "Region" aligns with the generic DefinedRegion class.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentBuilding: A structure used for official governmental functions. Also called PublicBuilding, StateFacility, AdministrativeBuilding. Examples: UK Parliament, White House, UK parliament.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentBuilding
chosen_type.justification: Matches the OIE type and the examples of UK Parliament and White House.

candidates.label: GovernmentBuilding
candidates.comment: A GovernmentBuilding is a civic structure that houses government operations or services. Also called public building, state edifice, official premises. Examples: city hall, parliament building, courthouse, post office. Distinct from GovernmentOffice, which is a specific type of organization within a government building.

candidates.label: LegislativeBuilding
candidates.comment: A LegislativeBuilding is a government building civic structure where legislative bodies meet and conduct their work. Also called capitol building, parliament house, assembly hall. Examples: the U.S. Capitol, a state capitol building, the Houses of Parliament. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Courthouse
candidates.comment: A Courthouse is a government building where legal cases are heard and judicial proceedings take place. Also called court building, hall of justice, judicial building. Examples: Supreme Court of the United States, Old Bailey, local county courthouse.

types.embedding_query_text: Facility: A place, piece of equipment, or structure designed for a particular purpose. Also called Installation, Plant, Complex. Examples: non‑existent nuclear power plant in Iran.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: A facility is a place; the generic Place class captures the concept.

mentions: non‑existent nuclear power plant in Iran

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

types.embedding_query_text: Camp: A temporary settlement of people, often for humanitarian or military purposes. Also called Encampment, RefugeeCamp, Base. Examples: refugee camp on the US‑Mexico border.

chosen_type.label: Accommodation
chosen_type.justification: A refugee camp is a type of accommodation.

mentions: refugee camp on the US‑Mexico border

candidates.label: Accommodation
candidates.comment: An Accommodation is a Place that can house human beings, such as a hotel room, camping pitch, or meeting room. Also called lodging, dwelling, living space, temporary residence. Examples: A hotel suite, a campsite, a vacation rental apartment, a conference room.

candidates.label: CampingPitch
candidates.comment: An individual outdoor space for overnight stay, typically part of a larger camping site or campground. Also called tent pitch, RV pitch, caravan pitch, campsite spot. Examples: Tent site #3 at Yosemite, RV spot at KOA, a designated area for a caravan. Distinct from Campground, which is the larger site containing multiple pitches.

candidates.label: Campground
candidates.comment: A Campground is a CivicStructure or place used for overnight outdoor stays, typically containing multiple individual camping pitches for tents or recreational vehicles. Also called camping site, campsite, RV park, caravan park. Examples: Yellowstone National Park Campground, KOA Campground, a local state park campsite. Distinct from Hotel, which provides indoor lodging.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: PlaceOfWorship
candidates.comment: A PlaceOfWorship is a civic structure or building used for religious services and spiritual activities. Also called religious building, house of worship, sanctuary. Examples: a church, a synagogue, a mosque, a temple. Distinct from Museum, which is for exhibiting artifacts.

types.embedding_query_text: Hospital: A health-care institution providing patient treatment with specialized staff and equipment. Also called MedicalCenter, Clinic, HealthcareFacility. Examples: fake hospital in Gaza with a bomb crater.

chosen_type.label: Hospital
chosen_type.justification: Exact match for the OIE type.

mentions: fake hospital in Gaza with a bomb crater

candidates.label: Hospital
candidates.comment: A Hospital is a civic structure and medical institution providing patient treatment with specialized medical and nursing staff and equipment. Also called medical center, clinic, healthcare facility. Examples: Mayo Clinic, Massachusetts General Hospital, a local emergency room.

candidates.label: MedicalClinic
candidates.comment: A medical business facility, often associated with a hospital, dedicated to specific diagnosis and/or healthcare, typically for outpatients but sometimes inpatients. Also called clinic, healthcare center, medical facility. Examples: a dermatology clinic, a walk-in clinic, a university health clinic, a family practice. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger institution providing comprehensive medical care.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: DiagnosticLab
candidates.comment: A medical organization that provides on-site or off-site diagnostic services, such as testing and analysis. Also called Medical laboratory, pathology lab, clinical lab, testing facility. Examples: Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, a hospital's pathology department. Distinct from MedicalClinic, which provides direct patient care and consultations.

candidates.label: VeterinaryCare
candidates.comment: A local business or organization providing medical services for animals. Also called vet clinic, animal hospital, veterinary practice. Examples: a local veterinary office, an emergency animal hospital, a mobile vet service.

types.embedding_query_text: Watermark: A subtle marker embedded in digital media to indicate origin or authenticity. Also called DigitalMark, SteganographicTag, Signature. Examples: invisible watermarks.

chosen_type.label: Watermark
chosen_type.definition: A subtle marker embedded in digital media to indicate origin or authenticity.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate directly models a watermark; DigitalDocument is the closest listed superclass.

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. Examples: a personal reminder in a digital format, a draft of an idea, a quick thought saved electronically. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is intended for public consumption.

candidates.label: DigitalDocumentPermission
candidates.comment: An intangible entity defining the access rights granted to a specific person or group for a particular digital document. Also called File permission, access control, document rights, sharing setting. Examples: "Read-only access for John Doe", "Edit permission for the Marketing Team", "View and comment access for all users". Distinct from DigitalDocumentPermissionType, which is an enumeration of possible permission types.

candidates.label: IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration
candidates.comment: IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration is a media enumeration of IPTC 'Digital Source' codes, providing information about the origin of a digital media object. Also called digital media source types, IPTC source codes, content origin categories. Examples: 'Original', 'Scanned Print', 'Digital Capture', 'Composite'.

candidates.label: MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of codes used to indicate the authenticity of a media object in the context of its publication or sharing, especially regarding manipulation. Also called media authenticity rating, manipulation type, content integrity code. Examples: "original media", "transformed media", "edited media", "staged media", "misleading context".

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A calendar day expressed in a standard format. Also called CalendarDate, Day, Timestamp. Examples: 31 July 2026.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: Exact match for the OIE type and the example date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: Imagery Examples: real satellite, aerial or 3D imagery, real satellite imagery, aerial imagery, 3D imagery.

chosen_type.label: ImageObject
chosen_type.justification: Imagery (satellite, aerial, 3D) is represented by ImageObject.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: GeospatialGeometry
candidates.comment: GeospatialGeometry is an Intangible supertype of GeoShape, designed to accommodate definitions from Geo-Spatial best practices. Also called spatial geometry, geographic feature. Examples: A GeoShape, a KML polygon, a GeoJSON object.

candidates.label: 3DModel
candidates.comment: A 3DModel, as a MediaObject under CreativeWork, represents some kind of three-dimensional content, which may have various digital encodings. Also called 3D content, digital model, virtual model. Examples: A CAD file of an engine part, a character model for a video game, a geospatial terrain model, an architectural rendering.

candidates.label: Photograph
candidates.comment: A Photograph, as a CreativeWork, is an image captured using a camera. Also called photo, picture, image. Examples: a portrait photograph, a landscape photo, a news photograph. Distinct from Painting, which is created with paint.

candidates.label: Map
candidates.comment: A creative work that visually represents an area, showing features like roads, cities, or terrain. Also called cartographic representation, geographical chart, atlas page. Examples: a road map, a topographic map, a subway map, a world atlas.

types.embedding_query_text: Tool Examples: external AI detection tools.

chosen_type.label: SoftwareApplication
chosen_type.justification: External AI detection tools are software applications.

candidates.label: ActionAccessSpecification
candidates.comment: An ActionAccessSpecification is an Intangible item detailing the requirements that must be met to perform a specific Action. Also called access requirements, action prerequisites, permission rules. Examples: "Requires login," "Subscription needed," "Age 18+," "Admin privileges."

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: APIReference
candidates.comment: APIReference, as a TechArticle under CreativeWork, provides documentation for application programming interfaces. Also called API documentation, developer reference, programming interface guide. Examples: Google Maps API documentation, Stripe API reference, Python `requests` library documentation.

candidates.label: UserPageVisits
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of visiting a web page. Also called page view, web visit, browsing activity. Examples: a user navigating to a product page, visiting a news article, browsing a website.

types.embedding_query_text: Image Examples: fake Google Earth images, community garden image.

chosen_type.label: ImageObject
chosen_type.justification: Both mentions refer to images; ImageObject is the appropriate class.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: ImageGallery
candidates.comment: An ImageGallery is a collection page web page type specifically designed to display a collection of images. Also called photo gallery, picture album, visual collection page. Examples: a wedding photo gallery, a portfolio of landscape images, a product image carousel. Distinct from VideoGallery, which displays videos, and MediaGallery, which is a more general type.

candidates.label: GatedResidenceCommunity
candidates.comment: A GatedResidenceCommunity is a Residence type that is a residential area with restricted access. Also called gated community, private estate. Examples: A luxury residential complex with controlled entry, a retirement community with security gates, a private housing development.

candidates.label: Photograph
candidates.comment: A Photograph, as a CreativeWork, is an image captured using a camera. Also called photo, picture, image. Examples: a portrait photograph, a landscape photo, a news photograph. Distinct from Painting, which is created with paint.

candidates.label: ImageObjectSnapshot
candidates.comment: An ImageObjectSnapshot is a specific, byte-for-byte identical version of an ImageObject, where identity is determined by the exact content including embedded metadata. Also called exact image copy, immutable image, content-identical image. Examples: a specific version of a digital photograph with its original EXIF data, a cryptographically hashed image file. Distinct from ImageObject, which is the general concept of an image file, not necessarily a specific, immutable version.

chosen_type.definition: A textual input that guides an AI system to generate content.
chosen_type.justification: No existing class fits; Prompt is a kind of CreativeWork.

candidates.label: Poster
candidates.comment: A Poster is a CreativeWork, typically a large, illustrated placard or announcement posted to advertise or publicize something. Also called placard, bill, advertisement. Examples: a movie poster, a concert poster, a political campaign poster, a scientific research poster.

candidates.label: PublicToilet
candidates.comment: A PublicToilet is a CivicStructure containing one or more toilets available for use by the general public, customers, or employees. Also called public restroom, public convenience, washroom. Examples: a toilet in a park, a restroom in a shopping mall, a public toilet facility at a train station, a highway rest stop bathroom.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: TaxiStand
candidates.comment: A civic structure or designated area where taxis wait for passengers. Also called cab stand, taxi rank, hack stand. Examples: a taxi stand at an airport, a designated taxi area outside a hotel, a street corner taxi queue.
